text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and it does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Some four million voters scattered in 46 countries are to go to the polls in Sunday's presidential elections.
- Croatia will have to wait until the autumn for the restart of negotiations on EU membership, according to a letter by the EU Ministerial Council president Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo.
- Germany's support for Croatia does not burden it, says former German Foreign Minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher in an interview.
- Following an attack on presidential candidate Vlado Gotovac, he will only be speaking at two rallies -- one in Split and the other in Zagreb.
- The coastal city of Split is the leader in drug-related deaths. Out of the total of some 50 such deaths a year, Split accounts for half.
- Dalmatia is expecting some 3.5 million overnight stays in the coming months, thus increasing the 1996 results by some 35 percent.
- The quarterly wages' report shows salaries have increased by 12.7 percent compared with the same period in 1996, while spending rose by 30 percent in the same period.
- An opinion poll conducted by an independent agency has shown that honesty tops the traits of the future president's character, while modesty is at the very bottom of the list.
- I would like to enter the second round of presidential elections, says SDP presidential candidate Zdravko Tomac in an interview.
- According to information obtained by Croatian diplomats through reliable sources, the UNTAES military contingent is to start withdrawing on July 15 and the operation will last about three months.
- Six people are arrested following the stoning of the Peace Train to Vukovar on Sunday.
- The Sibenik chief of police's BMW car is blown up by an unknown bomber. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
